optimal/api:
The Optimal API is the same API the console uses.
Everything a chat in the console does starts from these endpoints, and chats you create here show up in the console's **History**.

| | |
|---|---|
| Base URL | `https://optimal.miosa.ai/api/v1` |
| Auth | `Authorization: Bearer <Optimal token>` |
| Body | JSON with `Content-Type: application/json`, except attachment uploads |
| Errors | `{"error": "<code>", "details": "<message>"}` |

## Authentication

Optimal does not take your API key directly.
Your API key mints a short-lived **Optimal token** on the MIOSA API, and every Optimal call uses that token.

The API key needs the **Chat with Optimal and start runs** permission (`osa:write`).
To approve or reject Optimal's changes with the token, the key also needs **Approve or reject Optimal's changes** (`osa:approve`).
A key bound to one workspace can mint a token for that workspace only.

### Mint a workspace token

`POST https://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/optimal/workspace-token`

```bash
curl -s https://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/optimal/workspace-token \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MIOSA_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"workspace_id": "your_workspace_id"}'
```

```json
{
  "token": "eyJhbGciOi...",
  "expires_at": 1792771200,
  "can_decide_approvals": false,
  "scope": {
    "user_id": "...",
    "tenant_id": "...",
    "workspace_id": "your_workspace_id",
    "workspace_role": "admin"
  }
}
```

- The token lasts 10 minutes; `expires_at` is a Unix time in seconds.
  Mint a new one when a call answers `401`.
- Chats belong to the key's user and to the workspace in the token.

| Status | Code | When |
|---|---|---|
| 401 | `UNAUTHORIZED` | The API key is missing or revoked |
| 403 | `FORBIDDEN` | The key does not have `osa:write` |
| 403 | `WORKSPACE_FORBIDDEN` | The key's user is not a member of the workspace |
| 403 | `API_KEY_WORKSPACE_BOUND` | The key is bound to a different workspace |
| 403 | `API_KEY_NOT_ELIGIBLE` | The key is bound to a project or an end user |
| 422 | `WORKSPACE_REQUIRED` | `workspace_id` is missing |

### Mint an organization token

`POST https://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/optimal/org-token` takes no body.
It mints a token for an **All workspaces** chat, which reads every workspace the user belongs to and asks which one to use before changing anything.
A key bound to one workspace cannot mint it.

## Chats

A chat is called a session in the API.

### Create a chat

`POST /sessions`

```bash
curl -s https://optimal.miosa.ai/api/v1/sessions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"resume": false}'
```

```json
{
  "id": "your_chat_id",
  "status": "created",
  "machine": null,
  "workspace": { "id": "your_workspace_id", "rule": "This chat belongs to the workspace it was started in and never moves; its machines, memory and spend are that workspace's." },
  "pending_workspace": null,
  "turn": { "state": "idle", "turn_id": null, "started_at": null, "last_event_seq": 0 }
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `resume` | boolean | Send `false` to always start a fresh chat |
| `client_key` | string | Your own key for this chat; creating again with the same key resumes it (`status: "resumed"`) |
| `model` | string | Optional; the only value is `optimal` |

### List chats

`GET /sessions`

| Query | Description |
|---|---|
| `page`, `per_page` | Pagination; `per_page` is 20 by default, at most 100 |
| `view` | `mine` (default), `team` for shared chats, or `members` for owners and admins |

```json
{
  "sessions": [
    { "id": "your_chat_id", "title": "Landing page", "message_count": 6, "created_at": "2026-10-23T14:02:11Z", "visibility": "personal" }
  ],
  "count": 1,
  "page": 1,
  "per_page": 20
}
```

### Rename or share a chat

`PATCH /sessions/{id}` with any of:

| Field | Values |
|---|---|
| `title` | Text |
| `mode` | `ask`, `build`, `investigate` |
| `visibility` | `personal`, `team` |

### Delete a chat

`DELETE /sessions/{id}` deletes the chat and its messages for good, and answers `{"status": "deleted", "session_id": "..."}`.
Machines the chat used are not touched.

## Messages

### Send a message

`POST /sessions/{id}/message`

```bash
curl -s https://optimal.miosa.ai/api/v1/sessions/$CHAT/message \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message": "Why did my latest deployment fail?", "mode": "investigate", "client_message_id": "msg-001"}'
```

The call returns at once with `202`; the reply arrives on the [stream](/docs/optimal/api#streaming).

```json
{
  "status": "processing",
  "session_id": "your_chat_id",
  "turn_id": "msg-001",
  "client_message_id": "msg-001",
  "queued": false
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `message` | string | Required. The text to send |
| `mode` | string | `ask`, `build`, or `investigate` |
| `client_message_id` | string | 1 to 128 characters of letters, digits, `_`, `.`, `:`, or `-`. Sending the same id again answers `200` with `status: "duplicate"` instead of a second turn |
| `machine` | object | `{"resource_type": "sandbox" \| "computer", "resource_id": "..."}`: run this message on that machine |
| `confirm_switch` | boolean | `true` to move a chat that is already working on another machine |
| `attachments` | array | Attachment ids from [Attachments](/docs/optimal/api#attachments) |

A message sent while Optimal is working waits behind the current turn, and `queued` is `true`.
`DELETE /sessions/{id}/queued/{client_message_id}` removes it until it starts; after that the call answers `409 not_queued`.

### Read the transcript

`GET /sessions/{id}/messages`

```json
{
  "messages": [
    { "role": "user", "content": "Why did my latest deployment fail?", "timestamp": "2026-10-23T14:02:11Z" },
    { "role": "assistant", "content": "The build failed at npm install...", "timestamp": "2026-10-23T14:02:40Z" }
  ],
  "count": 2,
  "queued": [],
  "owner": { "id": "...", "label": "Ada" }
}
```

### Stop a reply

`POST /sessions/{id}/cancel` answers `{"status": "cancel_requested"}`.
When nothing is running it answers `404 not_running`.

## Streaming

`GET /sessions/{id}/stream` is a Server-Sent Events stream.

```bash
curl -N https://optimal.miosa.ai/api/v1/sessions/$CHAT/stream \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

- A browser `EventSource` cannot set headers, so this endpoint also takes the token as `?token=`.
  No other endpoint accepts a token in the URL.
- Every event has a numbered `id:`.
  Reconnect with the `Last-Event-ID` header, or `?last_event_id=`, to replay what you missed.
- A new reader with no id gets the turn in flight from its start; finished turns come from `GET /sessions/{id}/messages`.
- If the events you missed are gone, the stream sends `replay_gap`; read the transcript, then keep streaming.

The main events:

| Event | Data | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `connected` | `session_id` | The stream is open |
| `turn_start` | `turn_id` | Optimal started on a message |
| `streaming_token` | `text`, `message_id` | The next piece of the reply |
| `tool_call` | `name`, `phase` (`start` or `end`) | Optimal is using a tool |
| `permission_required` | the step that waits | A step needs approval; see [Approvals](/docs/optimal/api#approvals) |
| `agent_response` | `response` | The finished reply |
| `turn_billed` | `turn_credits`, `session_credits`, `balance` | What the turn cost, once the ledger settles |
| `replay_gap` | `session_id`, `last_seq` | Events you asked to replay are gone |

Ignore events you do not use; new events can be added.

## Machines

A chat can work on one sandbox or computer in your workspace at a time.

`POST /sessions/{id}/machine`

```json
{ "resource_type": "sandbox", "resource_id": "your_sandbox_id" }
```

Answers `{"session_id": "...", "machine": {"resource_type": "sandbox", "resource_id": "..."}}`.
`DELETE /sessions/{id}/machine` unbinds it; the machine keeps running.

| Status | Code | When |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_machine` | `resource_type` is not `sandbox` or `computer`, or `resource_id` is missing |
| 404 | `machine_not_found` | The machine is not in this workspace |
| 409 | `machine_unavailable` | The machine is not running or cannot be reached |
| 409 | `machine_switch_requires_confirmation` | The chat is working on another machine; send `confirm_switch: true` |

## Attachments

`POST /sessions/{id}/attachments?name={file_name}` takes the raw file bytes as the body.

```bash
curl -s "https://optimal.miosa.ai/api/v1/sessions/$CHAT/attachments?name=error.log" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/octet-stream" \
  --data-binary @error.log
```

```json
{ "id": "att_...", "name": "error.log", "mime": "text/plain", "bytes": 2048, "path": "/workspace/uploads/error.log", "vision": false }
```

Pass the `id` in the next message's `attachments`.
Files are up to 10 MB each and 25 MB per chat.
A file that is neither an image nor a document needs a machine bound to the chat, or the call answers `409 no_machine`.

## Approvals

`GET /approvals` lists approvals; filter with `session_id` and `status` (`pending`, `approved`, `rejected`).

```json
{ "approvals": [ { "id": "...", "status": "pending", "session_id": "your_chat_id", "title": "Delete sandbox api-old" } ], "count": 1 }
```

- `POST /approvals/{id}/approve` approves; `POST /approvals/{id}/reject` declines.
  Both take an optional `reason`.
- A token whose `can_decide_approvals` is `false` gets `403 approval_scope_required`.
- Deciding twice answers `409 already_decided`.

See [Approvals](/docs/optimal/approvals).

## Models

`GET /models` returns one model, `optimal`, with its live price:

```json
{
  "models": [
    {
      "id": "optimal",
      "name": "Optimal",
      "provider": "MIOSA",
      "context_window": 1048576,
      "default": true,
      "credits_per_1m": { "input": 150, "output": 600 },
      "pricing": {
        "unit": "wallet credits (1 credit = 1 cent)",
        "input_credits_per_1m": 150,
        "output_credits_per_1m": 600
      }
    }
  ],
  "current": "optimal",
  "default": "optimal",
  "currency": "wallet credits (1 credit = 1 cent)"
}
```

Any other `model` value answers `400 MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED`.

## A chat's cost

`GET https://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/credits/session/{chat_id}` is on the MIOSA API and takes your API key.

```json
{
  "session_id": "your_chat_id",
  "model_credits": 12,
  "machine_credits": 7,
  "total_credits": 19,
  "attributed": true,
  "settled": true,
  "as_of": "2026-10-23T14:10:00Z"
}
```

## Errors

| Status | Code | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `missing or empty message` | `message` is empty |
| 401 | `MISSING_TOKEN`, or an expired token | Mint a new Optimal token |
| 402 | `OPTIMAL_CREDITS_REQUIRED` | No credits left; add credits or upgrade |
| 403 | `ownership_denied` | The machine is not in your organization |
| 404 | `session_not_found` | The chat does not exist, or is not yours |
| 415 | `unsupported_media_type` | A JSON body without `Content-Type: application/json` |
| 429 | `rate_limited` | Too many requests; wait for `Retry-After` |
| 429 | `session_ceiling` | Too many chats running at once for your organization |

A chat in another organization or workspace answers `404`, the same as one that does not exist.

> **Note: Only what a chat needs**
>
> The Optimal token reaches chats, history, artifacts, investigations, approvals, cost, and settings.
> It cannot run tools directly or reach MIOSA's own servers.
> See [Isolation and permissions](/docs/optimal/isolation).
optimal/approvals:
Optimal asks before it acts.
When a step needs your decision, the chat pauses and an approval card appears above the composer.

## Approve or decline

An approval card names the step Optimal wants to take.

- **Approve** lets that one step run.
- **Decline** refuses it, and Optimal continues another way or tells you what it could not do.
- **Allow for this chat** approves it and lets the same kind of step run without asking for the rest of the chat.
  It shows only for steps that can be remembered.

When several cards are waiting, the newest shows first with "N more waiting".

## Choose what Optimal asks before

In **Preferences**, under **Approvals**, **Ask before** sets which steps wait for you in the workspace:

| Setting | Steps that wait |
|---|---|
| Every step | Every step that uses a tool |
| Changes only | Steps that change something |
| Deletions only | Steps that delete something |

The default is **Changes only**.
The setting is yours: it applies to your chats in this workspace, on every device.

## Auto-approve

The **Auto-approve** switch sits in the chat header of an Optimal chat.
When it is on, Optimal runs every tool it asks for in this workspace without stopping.
Turn it off to go back to the **Ask before** setting.

On an empty chat, the same switch sits under the composer.
Auto-approve is offered for the Optimal brain only.

## Allowed in this chat

Every step you allowed with **Allow for this chat** is listed under **...** > **Allowed in this chat (N)** in the chat header.
**Remove** puts a step back to asking.
When nothing is allowed, the list reads "Nothing is allowed without asking in this chat."

## Every pending approval

**Approvals** in the Optimal sidebar lists approvals across your chats in the workspace.
Each row says which chat it came from, and you can search the list.
A pending approval expires when the turn that asked for it ends.

## Signing in to a site

When Optimal needs to sign in to a site in its browser, it shows a secure sign-in card instead of asking in the chat.
What you type goes straight to the sign-in page and is not saved in the chat.
Tick **Save for next time** to keep the sign-in; saved sign-ins are listed in **Preferences** under **Sign-ins**, with a masked name only.
**Not now** skips it.

## Approvals over the API

An Optimal token minted from an API key can approve or reject only if the key has the **Approve or reject Optimal's changes** permission (`osa:approve`).
The token's `can_decide_approvals` field says whether it can.
Without it, the decision routes answer `403 approval_scope_required`, so a script cannot approve its own changes unless you allowed that.

```bash
# Pending approvals in one chat
curl -s "https://optimal.miosa.ai/api/v1/approvals?session_id=$CHAT&status=pending" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

# Approve one
curl -s -X POST https://optimal.miosa.ai/api/v1/approvals/$APPROVAL/approve \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"reason": "Looks right"}'
```

`/reject` declines.
Deciding twice answers `409 already_decided`.
See the [Optimal API](/docs/optimal/api#approvals).

> **Caution: Auto-approve follows you**
>
> Auto-approve and **Ask before** apply to your Optimal chats in the workspace, on every device.
> Platform policy still applies on top.

## Related

- [Isolation and permissions](/docs/optimal/isolation): what Optimal can reach at all.
- [Tasks, artifacts and history](/docs/optimal/workspace): the other Optimal sidebar pages.
optimal/brains:
The brain is who answers a chat.
Pick it in the composer's brain picker (tooltip "Choose who answers") before the first message.

## The three kinds of brain

| Brain | Billed to | Where it runs | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Optimal** | Wallet credits | MIOSA, working on your machines through scoped tools | Questions about your workspace, building, investigating |
| **A harness** | Your own model account | On the sandbox or computer you pick | Coding with Claude Code, Codex, OSA, and others |
| **A saved agent** | Your own model account | On the sandbox or computer you pick | An agent with your own instructions, tools, and permissions |

## Optimal

Optimal is the model built into MIOSA.
The picker shows it as "Built into MIOSA" and "Uses your wallet credits", with the live price under it.

- It is one model, with a 1M-token context.
- You cannot pick a different model for it, and it does not use your own model keys.
- It is the only brain that offers Investigate mode.

On the free plan with no credits left, Optimal is disabled in the picker with "Add credits to use Optimal".

## Harnesses

A harness is a coding agent that runs on a machine on your own account.
MIOSA credits never pay for its model.
The picker lists the harnesses under **Your agents**:

- Claude Code, Codex, and OSA;
- OpenCode, pi, Prime Agent, Kimi Code, Mistral Vibe, and Hermes, when your organization can connect them.

Each row shows its connection state: "Connected" with the account, "Not connected", or "Needs signing in again".
**Connect** or **Reconnect** opens the sign-in for that harness, then returns you to Optimal.
See [Harnesses and auth](/docs/agents/harnesses) for what each harness accepts.

A harness always asks where to work, in any mode, because each message is a run on a machine.
The cost strip says the work is billed to your own plan.

## Saved agents

A saved agent is an agent you built in Agent Studio, with its own instructions, harness, model, tools, and permissions.
Saved agents appear under **Your agents** next to the harness they use.
An archived agent is not listed.

To build one, choose **Build an agent** at the bottom of the brain picker, or open [Agent Studio](/docs/agents/agent-studio).
From the CLI:

```bash
miosa agent new reviewer --harness claude-code --instructions-file review.md
miosa agent list
```

## Switching brains

The brain is fixed after the first message.
The picker's tooltip then reads "This chat keeps its brain. Start a new chat to change it."
Picking another brain in a started chat starts a new chat.

> **Note: Your keys stay yours**
>
> Harnesses and saved agents run on your own model account.
> Optimal's model is MIOSA's, and is paid only in wallet credits.

## Related

- [Chat with an agent on a machine](/docs/agents/chat-on-a-machine): the same brains from a computer or sandbox page.
- [Agent confinement](/docs/agents/confinement): what an agent can reach from inside its machine.
- [Pricing and usage](/docs/optimal/pricing): how each brain is billed.
optimal/chats:
A chat is one conversation with one brain, in one workspace.
Open **Optimal** in the sidebar to reopen your most recent chat in the current workspace, or press **New** to start a fresh one.

## Pick a workspace first

Optimal works in one workspace at a time.
With a single workspace selected, the chat can read and change resources in that workspace only.

If **All workspaces** is selected, the chat reads every workspace you belong to.
It asks which workspace to use before it changes anything.

## The composer

The empty chat shows a headline for the current mode, three starter suggestions, and the composer.
From left to right, the composer toolbar has:

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **+** | Adds files or MIOSA resources to the chat as context |
| Mode menu | Switches between Ask, Build, and Investigate |
| Brain picker | Chooses who answers; see [Brains and agents](/docs/optimal/brains) |
| Machine menu | Chooses where Optimal works; shown in Build mode or once a machine is involved |
| **Send message** | Sends; while Optimal is working it becomes **Queue message** |
| **Stop** | Cancels the running reply |

Under the input, the cost strip shows what the chat has cost so far.
See [Pricing and usage](/docs/optimal/pricing).

## Modes

| Mode | Use it to | Starter suggestions |
|---|---|---|
| Ask | Get answers from live workspace context | "What needs my attention in this workspace?", "Summarize what changed in the last day" |
| Build | Build or change something on a sandbox or computer | "Build a landing page and publish it", "Build a small API with a database" |
| Investigate | Trace evidence before reaching a conclusion | "Why did my latest deployment fail?", "Trace the most recent error in my logs" |

You can change the mode between messages.
After an answer in Ask mode, **Switch to Build and run this** turns the answer into work on a machine.

Investigate always runs on the Optimal brain.
With a harness or saved agent as the brain, Investigate is not offered; start a new chat to use it.

## Add context

Press **+** to open **Add context**.
You can:

- attach files: images, documents, or any file, up to 10 MB each and 25 MB per chat;
- drop or paste files straight into the composer;
- point Optimal at MIOSA resources in your workspace.

Optimal takes three kinds of file:

| Kind | Examples | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| Image | PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF | The model sees it |
| Document | PDF, Word, Excel, CSV, Markdown, JSON, code | Its text is read into the message |
| Any other file | Archives, binaries | It is written to the chat's machine, under `/workspace/uploads` |

Any other file needs a machine bound to the chat; pick a sandbox or computer, then send again.
When the chat has a machine, images and documents are copied to it too.

## Send while Optimal works

You can keep typing while Optimal works.
**Queue message** sends your message right after the current reply finishes.
A queued message can be removed until it starts.

## Stop

**Stop** cancels the reply in progress.
The chat shows "Stopped", and what Optimal finished before you stopped it stays in the chat.

## Context and compaction

Every chat has a 1M-token context.
The context meter in the chat header shows how much is used, for example "312K of 1M context".
It turns amber at 70% and red at 90%.

When the context fills, Optimal folds the older part of the chat into a short summary on its own.
The meter shows "Compacting context..." while it does.
Nothing is needed from you.

## Rename, share, delete

The **...** menu in the chat header (tooltip "Chat options") has:

- **Rename**: gives the chat a new title.
- **Allowed in this chat**: lists the steps you allowed without asking, with **Remove** on each; see [Approvals](/docs/optimal/approvals).
- **Delete**: deletes the chat and its messages for good.
  Machines the chat used are not touched.

To share a chat with your team, use **Share with team** from its menu in **My chats**.
See [Team chats and sharing](/docs/optimal/team-chats).

## Ask Optimal from any page

On project, product, deployment, agent, workflow, computer, sandbox, database, and storage pages, the sidebar shows **Ask Optimal**.
It opens Optimal next to the page, with that page as context.
The shortcut is `Alt` + `Shift` + `O`.

## Find a chat again

**History** in the Optimal sidebar lists every chat in the workspace, with search and **Load older chats**.
Recent chats also sit in the sidebar under **Mine** and **Team**.
How long chats stay is set in **Preferences**: 30 days, 90 days, or 1 year.
See [Tasks, artifacts and history](/docs/optimal/workspace).

> **Note: A chat keeps its brain**
>
> The brain is fixed after the first message.
> Picking a different brain in a started chat starts a new chat.

## Related

- [Build on your machines](/docs/optimal/machines): the machine menu and the side panel.
- [Optimal API](/docs/optimal/api): the same chats over HTTP.
optimal/isolation:
Optimal acts only inside your organization and workspace, with your permissions.
It never reaches anything you could not reach yourself.

## Scoped per chat

Every key Optimal holds is scoped to one chat:

- a machine key bound to one sandbox or computer; or
- a workspace key bound to your organization, workspace, and user.

Both are minted per chat from the chat's saved scope, never from a message or a tool argument.
They are short-lived, and are never logged or saved in a tool result.

## Every call re-checks the scope

Each tool call re-derives your organization, workspace, and user from the chat.
An id in a tool argument is ignored.
A foreign organization, a sibling workspace, and an unknown id all get the same answer: not found, or no access.

## Nothing runs on MIOSA's host

For a hosted chat, no shell or file tool runs on the Optimal host.
Those tools run only on the machine the chat is bound to.
Tool output is cleaned before the model or the stream sees it.

## Dispatched agents get none of Optimal's authority

When Optimal dispatches a harness run, the run request carries no key, token, or scope.
The harness runs on your own account, and Optimal's own reasoning bills wallet credits.

- [Approvals](/docs/optimal/approvals): what Optimal asks before it acts.

optimal/machines:
Optimal does its building on a machine: a sandbox or a computer in your workspace.
You choose which one, and you can watch, steer, or take over at any time.

## Choose a machine

The machine menu sits in the composer toolbar.
It shows in Build mode, or once the chat has a machine.
Its label is **Auto** until you pick one, then the machine's name.

When you send a Build message and the chat has no machine, the menu opens on its own.
You can:

- pick **New sandbox**, with a size and its hourly price;
- pick **New computer**, with its hourly price;
- pick a machine you already have, under **Other machines in this workspace**.

A new sandbox has an idle timeout of 30 minutes.

A harness or saved agent always asks where to work, in any mode, because each message is a run on a machine.

## Machines in this chat

Under **This chat** the menu lists the chat's machines.
For each machine you can **Open** it, choose **Run next message here**, pause or resume it, stop it, or delete it.
**Add a sandbox** and **Add a computer** add another.

At the bottom of the menu:

| Action | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Pause all** | Pauses every machine in the chat |
| **Remove all** | Deletes every machine of the chat for good, after a confirm; their files are lost unless you took snapshots |
| **See all** | Opens the full machine list |
| **Show the preview** | Opens the Preview tab |
| **Detach from this chat** | Unbinds the machine; it keeps running |

If Optimal wants to move the chat to a different machine, it asks "Move this chat to ...?" with **Keep current** and **Move it**.

## The side panel

When work starts, the side panel opens on the right and follows the chat's machine.
Toggle it with **Open side panel** and **Close side panel**, and drag its edge to resize it.

| Tab | Shows |
|---|---|
| Preview | Your app, live from the machine |
| Browser | The live browser Optimal is using, from a sandbox |
| Desktop | The computer's live desktop |
| Machine | The sandbox or computer itself: its state, size, cost, and controls |
| Progress | What the agent is doing now and what it has finished |
| Terminal | A shell on the machine |
| Files | Browse and edit what is on the machine |
| Code | Every file changed in this chat, with its changes |
| Artifacts | Everything Optimal has produced for you |
| Deployments | Your sites and apps, and whether they are live |
| Logs | What the machine and its apps print |

A tab that does not apply yet shows what to do, for example "No computer in this chat" with **Add a computer**.

## Preview and publish

When Optimal serves an app, a preview card appears in the chat.
**Open preview** opens it; **Publish** puts it on a public URL.

The publish sheet asks for:

- **Update this site** or **New site**;
- the site name;
- the folder to publish, `/workspace` by default.

**Publish** creates the site and **Publish update** updates it.
The machine has to be running to publish.
The sheet also links to **Manage**, the custom domain, and recent versions.

## Stop, take over, hand back

- **Stop** cancels the running reply.
- **Take over**, on the Desktop and Browser tabs, pauses the agent and gives you the controls.
  The chat shows "You're in control".
- **Hand back** returns control, and the agent picks up from the machine's current state.

While you are in control, the agent cannot click or type.
If the agent asked you to take over, for example to finish a sign-in, it continues from where you leave the machine.

> **Tip: Watching without taking over**
>
> Clicking the desktop while you are only watching asks first.
> Choose **Keep watching** to stay hands-off.

## When the machine is gone

If the chat's machine is deleted, the chat says "This chat's machine was deleted. Pick another, or let Optimal choose."
Pick a machine in the machine menu and send again.

## Related

- [Chats and modes](/docs/optimal/chats): the composer and modes.
- [Isolation and permissions](/docs/optimal/isolation): what Optimal can touch on a machine.
- [Chat with an agent on a machine](/docs/agents/chat-on-a-machine): the same chat from a computer or sandbox page.
optimal/pricing:
An Optimal chat has two costs: the model and the machines it uses.
Both are paid from wallet credits, where 1 credit is 1 cent.

## The Optimal model

| | Price |
|---|---|
| Input | $1.90 per 1M tokens |
| Output | $8.00 per 1M tokens |
| A typical message | About 3 credits |

Billing is in whole credits.
The part of a credit left over from one call carries to the next, so small calls are not each rounded up.

Every chat has the full 1M-token context, with automatic compaction when it fills.
See [Chats and modes](/docs/optimal/chats#context-and-compaction).

The live price is also returned by the API in `GET /models`, under `pricing`.
See the [Optimal API](/docs/optimal/api#models).

## Machines

A sandbox or computer that Optimal creates or uses bills at its normal size price, while it runs.
A new sandbox that Optimal creates has a 30-minute idle timeout.
See [Pricing](/docs/pricing) for machine rates.

## Harnesses and saved agents

A harness or saved agent bills its model to your own account, never to MIOSA credits.
The cost strip says so, for example "Billed to your Claude plan".
The machine it runs on still bills in credits.

## The cost strip

The cost strip sits under the composer and updates while Optimal works.
For an Optimal chat it reads, for example:

```text
12 credits model · 7 credits machines · 19 credits so far · 4,180 left · Add credits
```

| Part | Meaning |
|---|---|
| model | Model calls settled for this chat |
| machines | Machines this chat ran, settled for this chat |
| so far | The two together |
| left | Your wallet balance, in credits |

A running machine settles every few minutes, so the machine figure catches up shortly after the work.
The (i) tooltip explains each figure.

## The Usage page

**Usage** in the Optimal sidebar shows Optimal's spend in the workspace:

- **Total cost**, **Tokens**, **Input**, and **Output**;
- your credit balance;
- **Model activity**: requests and cost for Optimal.

## When credits run out

Optimal needs a positive credit balance.
With no credits left, it does not start a chat or answer a message.
On the free plan, the chat shows "Optimal runs on credits" with **Upgrade** and **Add credits**.
Over the API, the call answers `402` with the code `OPTIMAL_CREDITS_REQUIRED`.

Add credits from **Billing**, or upgrade your plan, then send again.

> **Tip: One chat's cost from the API**
>
> `GET https://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/credits/session/{chat_id}` returns `model_credits`, `machine_credits`, and `total_credits` for one chat, read from the ledger.
> `attributed` is `false` when no machine has been tagged with the chat yet, so the total is the model only.

## Related

- [Pricing](/docs/pricing): every MIOSA price.
- [Brains and agents](/docs/optimal/brains): which brain bills where.
optimal/quickstart:
This walkthrough takes about five minutes.
You ask Optimal a question, have it build a page on a sandbox, and then send the same kind of message from your own code.

## Before you start

- A MIOSA account with a workspace.
- Wallet credits, or a paid plan.
  On the free plan with no credits left, the Optimal brain is disabled until you add credits.

## 1. Ask a question

1. Open **Optimal** in the console sidebar.
2. Pick a single workspace in the workspace switcher.
3. Leave the mode on **Ask** and choose the starter "What needs my attention in this workspace?", or type your own question.
4. Press **Send message**.

Optimal reads your live workspace and answers in the chat.
Ask mode never touches a machine.

## 2. Build something

1. Open the mode menu in the composer and pick **Build**.
2. Type "Build a landing page and publish it", then send.
3. Optimal asks where to build.
   In the machine menu, pick **New sandbox**, or pick a machine you already have.
4. The side panel opens.
   Watch **Progress** for the steps, and open **Preview** when the page is served.

Steps that change your workspace wait for your approval.
Press **Approve** on the card above the composer, or **Allow for this chat** to stop being asked for that kind of step in this chat.

When the page looks right, press **Publish** on the preview card to put it on a public URL.
See [Build on your machines](/docs/optimal/machines).

## 3. Send a message from code

Optimal has an HTTP API at `https://optimal.miosa.ai/api/v1`.
It takes a short-lived Optimal token, which your API key mints.

Create an API key with the **Chat with Optimal and start runs** permission (`osa:write`), then:

```bash
export MIOSA_API_KEY=msk_your_key
export WORKSPACE=your_workspace_id

# 1. Mint a 10-minute Optimal token for one workspace.
TOKEN=$(curl -s https://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/optimal/workspace-token \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MIOSA_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"workspace_id\": \"$WORKSPACE\"}" | jq -r .token)

# 2. Start a chat.
CHAT=$(curl -s https://optimal.miosa.ai/api/v1/sessions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"resume": false}' | jq -r .id)

# 3. Open the stream in the background, so you see the turn from its start.
curl -sN "https://optimal.miosa.ai/api/v1/sessions/$CHAT/stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" &

# 4. Send a message. This call returns at once with 202; the reply arrives on the stream.
curl -s https://optimal.miosa.ai/api/v1/sessions/$CHAT/message \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message": "Summarize what changed in the last day", "mode": "ask"}'
```

The stream sends `streaming_token` events while the reply is written and an `agent_response` event with the full reply.
`GET /sessions/$CHAT/messages` returns the finished transcript at any time.
The chat also appears in **History** in the console.
See the [Optimal API](/docs/optimal/api) for every endpoint.

> **Note: Tokens expire after 10 minutes**
>
> Mint a new Optimal token when a call answers `401`.
> The chat keeps going; only the token is new.

## Next

- [Chats and modes](/docs/optimal/chats): attachments, queued messages, and context.
- [Approvals](/docs/optimal/approvals): choose what Optimal asks before.
- [Pricing and usage](/docs/optimal/pricing): what a chat costs and where to see it.
optimal/team-chats:
A new Optimal chat is personal.
You can share it with everyone in its workspace, and turn it back into a personal chat at any time.

## Share a chat

From a chat's **...** menu in **My chats**:

- **Share with team** opens the chat to everyone in its workspace.
- **Make personal** makes it yours alone again.

## The chat lists

The sidebar's recent chats have tabs, and each opens a full list:

| List | What it shows |
|---|---|
| **My chats** | Your chats with Optimal. A personal chat is yours; a shared one is open to everyone in its workspace. |
| **Team chats** | Chats shared with everyone in the workspace. Anyone can read one and add a message; each message shows who wrote it. |
| **Team members** | Members' personal chats, by person. Shown to organization owners and admins only. |

Rows are marked when a chat is shared, when it is working, when it "Needs you", or when it is "Read only" for you.

## Writing in a shared chat

In a team chat, each message shows who wrote it.
A member who is not the chat's creator sends words only.
The chat's machine, brain, and files stay as its creator set them.

A workspace viewer can read team chats but not post in them.

## Owners and admins

Organization owners and admins can open **Team members** to read members' personal chats, and **Join** one to carry on in the same chat.
Reading and joining are both recorded, and the chat's creator is told when someone joins.

Each person can see who has opened their chats under "Who has opened my chats".
Owners and admins see their own record under "Recorded views of members' chats".

> **Note: Nothing hidden**
>
> **Preferences** says it plainly: "Your chats are personal until you share them with the team from a chat's menu. Organization owners and admins can view and join your chats."

## Related

- [Chats and modes](/docs/optimal/chats): renaming and deleting a chat.
- [Isolation and permissions](/docs/optimal/isolation): what a chat can reach.
optimal/troubleshooting:
Each entry starts with what you see, then the fix.

## In the console

### "Optimal runs on credits"

Optimal needs a positive credit balance, and yours is empty.
Press **Add credits**, or **Upgrade** for a plan with credits, then send again.
In the brain picker the same state reads "Add credits to use Optimal".

A harness or saved agent does not use credits for its model, so you can still use one of those.

### "Choose or create a workspace to start an isolated Optimal chat."

No workspace is selected.
Pick one in the workspace switcher.
Under **All workspaces**, Optimal reads every workspace but asks which one to use before it changes anything.

### Investigate is greyed out

Investigate always runs on the Optimal brain.
The chat's brain is a harness or a saved agent, and a chat keeps its brain.
Start a new chat with **New** and pick Optimal.

### The brain picker will not change

The brain is fixed after the first message.
Picking a different brain starts a new chat.

### A harness shows "Not connected" or "Needs signing in again"

Press **Connect** or **Reconnect** on its row in the brain picker, sign in, and you return to Optimal.
See [Harnesses and auth](/docs/agents/harnesses).

### "This chat's machine was deleted. Pick another, or let Optimal choose."

The sandbox or computer bound to the chat no longer exists.
Pick a machine in the machine menu, or send in Build mode and choose **New sandbox**.

### "... is kept on this chat's machine: pick a sandbox or computer, then send again."

The file is not an image or a document, so it is written to the chat's machine, and the chat has none.
Pick a machine in the machine menu, then send the file again.
Files are limited to 10 MB each and 25 MB per chat.

### "Interrupted. The reply stopped early."

The reply was cut off before it finished.
Press **Try again** next to the note; the chat keeps everything before it.

### "Couldn't take over. Try again." or "Couldn't hand it back. Try again."

The machine did not answer in time.
Wait a moment and press **Take over** or **Hand back** again.
Check the **Machine** tab to see that the machine is running.

### Publish is not available

The machine has to be running to publish.
Resume it from the **Machine** tab or the machine menu, then press **Publish** again.

### The context meter is red

The chat has used most of its 1M-token context.
Nothing is needed: Optimal folds the older part into a summary on its own and shows "Compacting context..." while it does.

## Over the API

| You get | Fix |
|---|---|
| `401` with `MISSING_TOKEN` | Send `Authorization: Bearer <Optimal token>`, not your API key |
| `401` on a call that worked before | The Optimal token expired after 10 minutes; mint a new one |
| `403 FORBIDDEN` when minting | Give the API key the `osa:write` permission |
| `403 API_KEY_WORKSPACE_BOUND` | Mint the token for the workspace the key is bound to |
| `403 approval_scope_required` | Give the API key the `osa:approve` permission, then mint a new token |
| `402 OPTIMAL_CREDITS_REQUIRED` | Add credits or upgrade |
| `404 session_not_found` | The chat id is wrong, deleted, or in another workspace; check the token's workspace |
| `409 machine_switch_requires_confirmation` | Send the message again with `"confirm_switch": true` |
| `409 machine_unavailable` | Start the machine, then retry |
| `409 no_machine` on an upload | Bind a machine with `POST /sessions/{id}/machine` first |
| `415 unsupported_media_type` | Add `Content-Type: application/json` |
| `429 rate_limited` | Wait for the `Retry-After` seconds |
| A stream that shows nothing | Open the stream before you send, or read finished turns from `GET /sessions/{id}/messages` |

See the [Optimal API](/docs/optimal/api) for every endpoint.

## Related

- [Pricing and usage](/docs/optimal/pricing): credits and what a chat costs.
- [Build on your machines](/docs/optimal/machines): the machine menu and side panel.
- [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting): problems outside Optimal.
optimal/workspace:
Inside Optimal, the sidebar switches to Optimal's own pages.
Each page shows the current workspace.

| Page | What it keeps |
|---|---|
| **New** | Starts a fresh chat |
| **Tasks** | What Optimal took on in your chats, grouped by chat |
| **Investigations** | The investigations Optimal ran, with their evidence |
| **Artifacts** | Everything Optimal produced for you |
| **Approvals** | Approvals across your chats; see [Approvals](/docs/optimal/approvals) |
| **History** | Every chat, and what Optimal did in the workspace |
| **Usage** | Spend and tokens; see [Pricing and usage](/docs/optimal/pricing) |
| **Preferences** | Approvals, memory, chat history, notifications, and sign-ins |

## Tasks

Tasks lists what Optimal took on, grouped by the chat it came from.
The page refreshes while something is still running.
A running group of tasks can be cancelled from here.

When there are none yet, the page reads "No durable tasks yet".
Ask Optimal to investigate, plan, or operate something and its task appears.

## Investigations and Artifacts

Both pages have a search box and a status filter.

- **Review investigation** opens an investigation and the evidence behind it.
- **Open artifact** opens something Optimal produced, such as a report or a file.

When a list is empty, **Start in Optimal** opens a new chat.

## History

History lists every chat in the workspace.
Search by title, open a chat to pick it up again, or use **Load older chats** to go further back.
Each row has a menu to rename or delete the chat, and **Copy chat ID**.

Below the chats, **Workspace events** lists what Optimal did in the workspace.

## Preferences

| Section | Setting | Options |
|---|---|---|
| Approvals | Ask before | Every step, Changes only, Deletions only |
| About you | Remember across chats | On or off; your saved memories are listed with **Delete** |
| Chat history | Keep chats for | 30 days, 90 days, 1 year |
| Notifications | Needs your approval, Work finished | On or off |
| Sign-ins | Saved sign-ins | Masked site names, with **Remove** |

Memories are yours: only you see them, and only in this workspace.
Turn **Remember across chats** off to stop Optimal keeping new ones.

Chats older than the **Keep chats for** setting can no longer be resumed.

## Related

- [Chats and modes](/docs/optimal/chats): working in a single chat.
- [Team chats and sharing](/docs/optimal/team-chats): sharing chats with your workspace.
